hero.eyebrowSuffix: · Partner-scoped REST API · Powered by PYXIS-1
hero.title: Put similarity and track intelligence [[inside your product.]]
hero.sub: Search your own catalogue by sound and rank it by how the music actually sounds, through a partner-scoped REST API. Structured Track Intelligence analysis is enabled on request, against your own catalogue.
hero.trustline: Partner-scoped · Versioned JSON · Private catalogue index
hero.routerLabel: Request router · One request enters, sonic intelligence returns
hero.routerAlt: Request router diagram: a developer request with a bearer key enters from the left and passes through a single scoped gate into the partner's private catalogue boundary. Inside, live routes for search and similarity process the request against the partner's own index, and structured JSON returns on the right. An analysis route is drawn as available on request, a playback route is drawn permission-gated, and there is no connection to any shared public catalogue. Fictional data.
hero.routerFoot: no shared partner catalogue exists on this diagram, or in the product

capabilities.title: Three capabilities. One partner-scoped API.

lanes.question: "Find the partner-catalogue track ID for this title or artist."
"Which tracks in our catalogue sound most like this one?"
lanes.ioIn: catalogue track ID · or uploaded reference (≤100 MB)
lanes.ioOut: ranked matches · scores · metadata · playlist info

lanes.question: "What does this track contain and how does it behave?"

capabilities.footnote: result depths: 10 · 20 · 50 · 100. Full parameters and schemas live at api-docs.resomix.com
capabilities.partialFieldsNote: Search and similarity are enabled on every partner key. Track analysis is provisioned on request and runs against your own catalogue, so talk to us before building on it. Returned fields are versioned and may be partial or optional.

isolation.title: Your key searches your catalogue. Nothing else.
isolation.diagramLabel: Partner isolation · Two partners, two sealed indexes
isolation.mobileContrast: No shared catalogue. No cross-partner results.
isolation.disclosureBody: Every partner runs against its own sealed index: its own catalogue, credentials and results. A key can never query another partner's catalogue or Resomix's consumer product, and an uploaded reference is only ever a query against your own index.

points.body: Each partner has its own catalogue, credentials, index and results.
A key can never query another partner's catalogue, or Resomix's consumer product.
An uploaded reference is analysed as the query; its matches still come only from your own indexed catalogue.

ingestion.title: Deliver the catalogue once. Query it through the API.
ingestion.lead: The API searches a private index built from your catalogue. Managed batch ingestion is the live onboarding route today.
mobileSteps: Private index ready, webhook notifies you
ingestion.mobileNote: audio + csv manifest → .done marker last → webhook when ready

checks.title: missing audio file
checks.body: manifest row 214 references a file not present in the batch, so the batch is rejected and the row is named in the report

checks.title: duplicate isrc
checks.body: two rows share one ISRC, so the batch is rejected and both rows are named in the report

checks.title: unsafe archive
checks.body: zip failed safety checks, so it is rejected before processing and the partner notified

ingestion.formats: accepted audio: .mp3 · .wav · .flac · .aiff; required manifest columns: isrc · title · display_artist · audio_filename; optional: bpm · duration_ms · genre · musical_key · release_date · upc_ean and more
ingestion.footnote: a partial upload never starts processing · .done is sent last · one active batch per partner · validation is all-or-nothing, so a rejected batch is corrected and re-sent with a new .done · new batches top up the catalogue and rebuild the private index

schema.title: Turn audio into versioned product data.
schema.defensiveBody: Fields may be optional: a partial result returns the fields that completed successfully, with the job status alongside.

liveRows.title: REST API

evaluate.title: Test the API on your own catalogue.
evaluate.lead: There is no public sandbox today. The current evaluation path is a guided pilot using a representative sample of your own catalogue.
evaluate.sandboxClosed: Why is there no public sandbox? ▸
evaluate.sandboxOpen: Why is there no public sandbox? ▾
evaluate.sandboxBold: Similarity is only meaningful inside a real catalogue.
evaluate.sandboxBody: A shared demo pool would misrepresent both the isolation model and the results you would see in production. The guided pilot puts a scoped key against your own repertoire instead: the same API, honest results. A self-serve trial catalogue is planned.
